label: FS AP-N506 Wi-Fi 6 indoor access point
description: FS AP-N506 - Wi-Fi 6 (802.11ax) indoor access point, dual radio 2x2 MU-MIMO, up to 1.8 Gbps aggregate, 256 clients (64 concurrent), 32 SSIDs, 2x 100/1000Base-T Ethernet, 802.3af/at PoE or 12V/1A DC, IP30, ceiling or wall mount.
notes:
Ports and power come from the **comparison table on the FS product pages**, which is the only place these APs publish a port census at all: the product page itself renders marketing copy for a keyless fetch, and the datasheet URLs 404. The table's **column order follows the page you are on** - the page's own product is column 1 and the rest keep catalogue order (N716, N516, N506, N506H, T566D) - which is worth knowing before reading a row across. **Gigabit only, and only two of them:** '2x 100/1000Base-T Ethernet Port'. The 1.8 Gbps aggregate is the radio's, not the wire's - a lab that expects 2.5G here because the N516 has it will be wrong, which is why the two models are separate files. Power: 'IEEE 802.3 af/at PoE, DC 12V/1A' - the only member of the family that an 802.3af injector can feed on its own rating. 256 max clients, 64 concurrent, 32 SSIDs, IP30.

The AP power inlet carries no wattage: the vendor publishes the PoE **class** and a DC input rating ('DC 12V/2A' is the adapter's rating, not a draw), so no `poeIn` figure is invented. `poeIn: 0` on the other sockets keeps the engine from treating a downlink port as a power inlet.
